name: Button
code:
from picozero import Button

button = Button(10)

pressed = button.is_pressed
note: pressed is True or False. No resistor is needed — picozero switches on the pin's own pull-up. Also button.when_pressed and button.when_released .
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico wired to a push button on a breadboard

name: Capacitive touch
code:
from picozero import TouchSensor

touch = TouchSensor(17)

touched = touch.is_touched
note: The TTP223 output goes high while touched. touched is True or False.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico connected to a TTP223 capacitive touch module

name: Potentiometer
code:
from picozero import Pot

pot = Pot(26)

setting = pot.value
note: setting runs from 0 to 1. Read pot.value again after turning; pot.voltage gives volts. Power the trimpot from 3V3 .
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico connected to a 3386P trimpot with its offset wiper on GP26

name: LDR
code:
from picozero import AnalogInputDevice

ldr = AnalogInputDevice(27)

light = ldr.value
note: light runs from 0 in the dark to 1 in bright light. Also ldr.voltage .
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico wired to an LDR and a 10 kilohm resistor on a breadboard

name: Distance sensor
code:
from picozero import DistanceSensor

sensor = DistanceSensor(
    echo=21, trigger=20
)

distance = sensor.distance
note: distance is in metres and stops at 1. Pass max_distance=2 to see further, or read sensor.value for 0 to 1. Use an HC-SR04P , powered from 3V3 .
wiringAlt: Four-pin HC-SR04P ultrasonic distance sensor wired to a Raspberry Pi Pico on a breadboard, with 3V3 and ground from the top rails

name: Tilt switch
code:
from picozero import Switch

tilt = Switch(8)

tilted = tilt.is_open
note: The reading may flicker while the ball rolls. Check it more than once before treating it as a definite tilt.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico connected to a tilt switch on a breadboard

name: Line sensor
code:
from picozero import DigitalInputDevice

line = DigitalInputDevice(18, pull_up=False)

on_line = line.is_active
note: Turn the blue adjuster until the module's output changes cleanly at the edge of the line.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico connected to a KY-033 line sensor

name: Toggle switch
code:
from picozero import Switch

mode = Switch(6)

mode_two = mode.is_closed
note: Connect COM and one outside pin. The unused outside pin can be left unconnected.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico connected to an SPDT toggle switch

name: Temperature sensor
code:
from picozero import TemperatureSensor

convert = lambda voltage: (voltage - 0.5) * 100
sensor = TemperatureSensor(28, conversion=convert)

temperature = sensor.temp
note: Read the TMP36 with its flat face towards you; the pins are +Vs, Vout, GND from left to right.
wiringAlt: TMP36 temperature sensor connected to Raspberry Pi Pico

name: Temperature probe
code:
from machine import Pin
import onewire, ds18x20
from time import sleep_ms

bus = onewire.OneWire(Pin(22))
sensor = ds18x20.DS18X20(bus)
probes = sensor.scan()
assert probes, "Check probe wiring"
sensor.convert_temp()
sleep_ms(750)
temperature = sensor.read_temp(probes[0])
print(temperature)
note: Repeat the conversion and 750 ms wait for each new reading.
wiringAlt: DS18B20 probe wired to 3V3 OUT pin 36, GP22 pin 29 and GND pin 28, with a 4.7 kilohm pull-up resistor

name: Active buzzer
code:
from picozero import Buzzer

buzzer = Buzzer(9)

buzzer.on()
note: Also buzzer.off() , buzzer.toggle() and buzzer.beep() . Give beep() an on_time and an off_time to set the rhythm. Faster beeps do not mean a higher pitch.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico wired to an active buzzer on a breadboard

name: Passive buzzer
code:
from picozero import PWMBuzzer

# GP9, 2000 Hz, 50% duty
buzzer = PWMBuzzer(9, 2000, 32768)

buzzer.on()
note: Try buzzer.freq = 1000 ; silence with buzzer.off() . Higher frequency means higher pitch. Beep speed is separate; both types can make rhythms.
wiringAlt: Raspberry Pi Pico GP9 and ground connected to a small passive piezo buzzer

name: LED
code:
from picozero import LED

led = LED(11)

led.on()
note: Use a 220 Ω resistor in series; led.off() turns it off.
wiringAlt: Pico GP11 connected through a resistor to an LED and GND

name: RGB LED
code:
from picozero import RGBLED

light = RGBLED(red=3, green=4, blue=5)

light.color = (255, 0, 255)
note: Common cathode to GND; each colour has its own 220 Ω resistor.
wiringAlt: Pico GP3, GP4 and GP5 connected through three resistors to an RGB LED
